compiled_state.title: DSO process: production-env-dependent code ships with dev-only test fixtures -> chain of prod-only defects each unblocking the next
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** 169451977a1cf1f5b063bd7005305e83663840ac
* **Scope:** DSO planning, implementation, and validation processes (cross-cutting; not a single module).
* **Concrete corpus:** epic 4047-3cb1-6cb4-46a1 (Derivable level-triggered Jira reconciler). Three child bugs (5be7-d657-1dde-4237, 96c5-03c6-338f-483f, bbf0-3380-74ab-4200) all instances of the same defect class — see Section 2.
* **NOT in scope of this bug:** fixing the three example defects. They each have their own ticket; bbf0 is open at filing time. This bug is about the planning/implementation/validation process gaps that let all three ship with full epic P1=PASS verdicts.

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** Process / planning / validation gap surfaced by dogfooding (the audit-live runbook flow on epic 4047).

#### Expected Behavior

The DSO workflow (preplanning → implementation-plan → sprint → completion-verifier → deep-tier review → CI llm-review) should produce code whose first contact with the live production runtime environment either succeeds or fails for a reason that no available pre-merge signal could have caught. When an epic ships a VALIDATION-CLASS Success Criterion (LIVE VERIFIED evidence), the planning + implementation + validation pipeline should produce a test that exercises the production-environment runtime constraints, not just dev-environment-equivalent unit fixtures.

#### Actual Behavior

Epic 4047 closed with verifier P1=PASS on all 11 stories and 12/12 SCs satisfied per the orchestrator's deep-tier review (3 sonnet specialists + opus arch synthesizer). PR #345 merged to main. Then the FIRST post-merge dry-run against the live CI environment surfaced three production-only defects, each unblocking the next:

| # | Bug | Surface | What the test fixture happened to satisfy that CI does not |
|---|-----|---------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1 | 5be7-d657-1dde-4237 | `__main__.py:151` leaves `repo_root=None` when --repo-root omitted; `git -C None ...` exit 128 | test_reconcile_main.py ALWAYS passes `--repo-root str(tmp_path)` and stubs the entire advisory_lock module |
| 2 | 96c5-03c6-338f-483f | `git worktree add <path> tickets` exit 128 because `.tickets-tracker` already owns the branch in a sibling worktree | test_advisory_lock.py creates `tickets` via `--orphan` and switches back to main — NEVER mounts tickets in a sibling worktree |
| 3 | bbf0-3380-74ab-4200 | `git commit` inside temp worktree exit 128 because CI runner has no `user.name`/`user.email` | tmp_path repos on dev machines inherit the developer's global git config — the test never runs in a config-isolated HOME |

All three are instances of the **same anti-pattern**:

> Production code makes runtime-environment assumptions (a CLI flag is always passed, no sibling worktree owns the target branch, global git config has user identity) that the unit-test fixture happens to satisfy on developer machines but the real CI runner does not.

The chain is informative: fixing each defect unblocks the next, because the test fixture for the next layer down ALSO doesn't reflect the production environment.

### 3. Action History — pipeline stages that should have caught this and did not

Each row below is a stage in the DSO pipeline that COULD have surfaced the defect class before merge, but did not.

| Stage | What it does | Why it missed |
|-------|-------------|---------------|
| `/dso:brainstorm` (epic scoping) | Surfaces scrutiny / preplanning concerns | The epic spec calls SCs 11/12 LIVE VERIFIED but the brainstorm didn't escalate "no integration test exists for advisory_lock's real-git path" as a scrutiny finding |
| `/dso:preplanning` (Done Definitions) | Each story carries DDs that the verifier audits | The advisory_lock story (a2ba) had unit-test DDs (each function returns expected value); no DD required a production-environment-faithful integration test |
| `/dso:implementation-plan` (task decomposition) | RED tests for each task | red-test-writer wrote tests against the dev-shaped fixture; no task spec required "test must pass with no global git config and no pre-mounted worktree" |
| `/dso:sprint` execution | Sub-agents implement tasks | Implementation sub-agents wrote unit-stubbed tests that happened to pass on dev; no instruction to test the production environment shape |
| Deep-tier review (3 specialists + opus arch) | Local review on the diff | Verification reviewer DID flag related concerns (V1 false-green contract test, V3 missing .test-index entries) but didn't escalate "the entire advisory_lock module is unverified against a real-git CI environment" — the meta-finding |
| CI llm-review | Strategy F large-diff path | Crashed on a 134KB non-JSON output (separately filed as dc47-ddf2-8b28-436d); even if it had succeeded, would likely have inherited the same blind spot |
| Completion-verifier (story-level + epic-level) | Checks DD evidence | Operates on what the DDs declare; the DDs didn't require live-environment fidelity, so the verifier had nothing to check |
| Pre-merge CI checks | Lint + unit tests + script tests | All passed; none exercise the production environment |
| **Live dry-run (after merge)** | First contact with real CI environment | Surfaced 5be7. After 5be7 fix → surfaced 96c5. After 96c5 fix → surfaced bbf0. Each fix takes a separate PR + merge + retrigger cycle. |

The defect class is **emergent** at every stage that could have caught it. It is not a single skill or agent's failure — it is a systemic gap.

### 4. Suspected Categories

* **Planning gap:** preplanning's story decomposition allows a VALIDATION-CLASS SC (epic-level claim of LIVE VERIFIED) to ship with only unit-test DDs. There is no required mapping from "epic SC asserts live evidence" to "at least one story Done Definition exercises the live-environment shape".
* **Implementation gap:** the behavioral-testing-standard prohibits change-detector tests and requires "observable behavior" but does not require coverage of "environment-state-absent" cases (no global git config, no pre-existing worktrees, no env vars set). Implementation agents default to fixture-based tests that work on dev because the standard does not require otherwise.
* **Review gap:** deep-tier code reviewers DID flag adjacent test-quality concerns but treated each one as a local finding. None escalated to the structural observation "this module is fundamentally unverified against the real production environment". The arch synthesizer's job is to find cross-cutting patterns, but it was framed around the diff, not against the production-environment surface.
* **Validation gap:** epic completion-verifier accepts `closure_checks_results` deferred to operator runbook for LIVE-VERIFIED criteria. The epic closes P1=PASS on implementation deliverables alone; the live evidence is deferred to "operator-driven rollout". This makes the live verification a post-merge surface, by design — which is correct for some classes of epic (you cannot fire test alerts in CI for a P0 alerting story) but creates a class of false-positive epic closures for VALIDATION-CLASS epics where the live evidence is the load-bearing claim.

### 5. Skills and Workflows Touched

* `/dso:brainstorm` — preplanning gates, scrutiny pipeline
* `/dso:preplanning` — story-decomposer; Done Definition rubric; closure-check rubric
* `/dso:implementation-plan` — task decomposition; testing-mode classification (RED / UPDATE / GREEN)
* `/dso:sprint` — completion-verifier dispatch protocol
* `/dso:review` (REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md) — deep-tier reviewer prompts; specifically code-reviewer-deep-verification + code-reviewer-deep-arch
* `/Users/joeoakhart/.claude/plugins/cache/digital-service-orchestra/dso-dev/1.17.51/skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md` — the 5-rule testing standard
* `agents/completion-verifier.md` — VALIDATION-CLASS handling
* CI workflow `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` — concrete corpus example

### 6. Logs and Evidence

Three child bug tickets with verbatim CI stack traces and reproduction commands:
* 5be7-d657-1dde-4237 (CLOSED — fixed PR #352)
* 96c5-03c6-338f-483f (CLOSED — fixed PR #354)
* bbf0-3380-74ab-4200 (OPEN — open at filing)

Failed CI runs:
* https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/26420646190 (5be7 surface)
* https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/26422283057 (96c5 surface)
* https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/actions/runs/26423439381 (bbf0 surface)

Epic 4047 verifier output (P1=PASS, 12/12 SCs) — recorded in epic comments — illustrates the validation-gap signature: every stage of the DSO pipeline reported success while the actual production-environment surface was untested.

#### Suggested remediation directions

The bug is the GAP. Remediation should address ALL of the following (each is a separate piece of work but they reinforce each other):

1. **Preplanning rubric amendment** — when an epic has any LIVE-VERIFIED or VALIDATION-CLASS SC, story-decomposer must emit at least one story whose Done Definition explicitly says "an integration test runs the implementation in a configuration-isolated environment (e.g., HOME=/tmp/fake-home, no pre-existing worktrees, no env vars set) and asserts the production path is reachable". Add this to `agents/story-decomposer.md` rubric.

2. **Behavioral-testing-standard amendment** — add a sixth rule: "Environment-state-absent coverage. When the code under test consumes runtime environment state (git config, mounted worktrees, env vars, file/directory presence outside tmp_path), the test suite must include at least one case where that state is explicitly absent and the code's expected behavior is documented." Update `skills/shared/prompts/behavioral-testing-standard.md`.

3. **Deep-tier reviewer prompt amendment** — add a verification-tier prompt question: "Identify any test in the diff that ASSUMES the host environment provides state the production CI/runtime does not (a developer's global git config, a sibling worktree, an unset env var that's actually set on the developer's machine). Flag as a test-environment-divergence finding even when the test passes." Update the dso:code-reviewer-deep-verification + dso:code-reviewer-deep-arch agent prompts.

4. **Completion-verifier amendment for VALIDATION-CLASS epics** — when an epic carries LIVE-VERIFIED SCs, the verifier should require either (a) a live-environment dry-run attached to the epic as evidence before P1=PASS, OR (b) explicit deferral with a named operator owner and a tracked follow-up ticket. Today the deferral path is implicit; no follow-up tracking exists.

5. **Anti-pattern detection scan addition** — add a Phase G anti-pattern scan rule to `/dso:fix-bug` for the "test fixture inherits dev-machine state" pattern: grep for tests that create tmp_path git repos without setting HOME, that use subprocess on git without explicit user.name/email, that don't mount sibling worktrees when the production code uses worktree-add — and flag any match for review.

6. **(Out of scope; mention only)** A real-git CI-like integration harness — set up a CI-equivalent test environment (a docker image with a fresh git, no global config, no pre-existing state) and run a curated set of "real-runtime" tests on it as a separate CI job. This is the heavy version of #2 above. Reserve for a follow-up epic if the lighter fixes (1–5) don't close the class.

This bug is not "fix the three examples" — those are addressed by their own tickets. This bug is about the PIPELINE failing to surface the class.

comments.body:
## Corpus update — chain extended

Two more instances of the defect class have surfaced since this bug was filed. The corpus now stands at FIVE concrete defects, all in the same chain:

| # | Bug | Surface | PR | Status |
|---|-----|---------|----|--------|
| 1 | 5be7-d657-1dde-4237 | `repo_root=None` propagation | #352 | Closed |
| 2 | 96c5-03c6-338f-483f | `git worktree add` dual-checkout | #354 | Closed |
| 3 | bbf0-3380-74ab-4200 | `git commit` no identity | #358 | Closed |
| 4 | 5b1c-a83c-3acc-4858 | `_try_load_step` omits sys.modules registration → Py 3.14 dataclass crash | #362 | Open |
| 5 | (unfiled) | `'Mutation' object has no attribute 'get'` at `applier.py:331` | — | Surfaced locally after #5b1c fix; next to file once #362 merges |

## Pattern prediction now empirically validated

When this bug was filed, the prediction "each fix in the chain unblocks the next defect of the same class" was structural reasoning from 3 data points. We now have 5 data points, with defect #5 surfacing locally **without needing another CI cycle** — the moment the #4 fix was applied, the next defect appeared in the same `python3 -m dso_reconciler --mode=dry-run` invocation. The chain is real.

## Specific reinforcement of remediation directions

**Direction #3 (deep-tier reviewer prompt amendment) is strongly validated by defect #4 (5b1c):**

The deep-tier review on PR #345 produced Cluster A which consolidated `sys.modules` keys for `mode`, `mutation`, `advisory_lock`, and `invariants`. The reviewer identified the class of defect correctly. BUT the consolidation **stopped at four modules**. The same package has THREE sibling-loader helpers (`_load_sibling_keyed`, `_try_load_step`, `_load`) — only ONE (`_load_sibling_keyed`) consistently registers in `sys.modules`. The other two have asymmetric behavior that the reviewer didn't audit for symmetry.

A deep-tier verification reviewer prompt addition such as:

> When you identify a sys.modules-registration / module-loader / import-machinery defect class, check whether the codebase has OTHER loader helpers in the same package — and if so, audit each one for the same defect. Flag partial consolidation as a finding even when the consolidation correctly addresses the loaders it touches.

would have caught defect #4 pre-merge.

**Direction #6 (real-git CI harness) is strongly validated by defects #1, #4, and #5:**

Defects #1, #4, and #5 are all reproducible locally in **three lines**:

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'plugins/dso/scripts')
import dso_reconciler.__main__ as main_mod
sys.argv = ['dso_reconciler', '--mode=dry-run', '--repo-root', '.']
rc = main_mod.main()
assert rc == 0
```

That test, run on Python 3.14 with `HOME=/tmp/fake-home` and no pre-mounted worktree, would have caught:
- #1 (repo_root=None) — argv has no --repo-root
- #4 (sys.modules registration) — Python 3.14 dataclass type-resolution fires on real run
- #5 (Mutation `.get`) — runs the actual reconcile_once code path

Defects #2 and #3 need the dual-worktree + isolated-HOME setup that the original Direction #6 already described. So:

* **3 of 5 defects** would have been caught by the minimal test above
* **5 of 5 defects** would have been caught by the full real-git CI harness

Direction #6 is no longer a "reserve for follow-up epic if lighter fixes don't close the class" suggestion — it's the highest-leverage single fix. Recommend promoting it from "out of scope" to "first remediation track."

## Additional observation: deep-tier review explicitly scoped out defect #5

The deep-tier verification reviewer on PR #345 explicitly noted defect #5's pattern (`'Mutation' object has no attribute 'get'`) as a "pre-existing baseline failure (test_reconcile_once + test_main_entry::test_run_pass_returns_75_on_reschedule_error) — out of scope, pre-existing baseline confirmed by `git stash` comparison; not caused by this work" — and accepted the epic for closure on that basis.

This is the smoking gun for the validation-gap claim in this bug. The deep-tier reviewer:
1. **Correctly identified** that 5 tests were failing
2. **Correctly identified** that those failures predate the diff under review
3. **Incorrectly inferred** that they were therefore safe to ship

The "pre-existing failure" framing treats test failures as belonging to the WORK that introduced them, not to the SYSTEM that ships them. When pre-existing test failures are in load-bearing code paths for a VALIDATION-CLASS epic, they ARE the epic's bug.

A deep-tier reviewer prompt addition such as:

> Pre-existing test failures in load-bearing code paths of a VALIDATION-CLASS epic are blocking findings for THIS epic, even if they were not introduced by the diff under review. List every test the diff does NOT cause to pass and assess: does the LIVE-VERIFIED claim survive these tests failing? If no, escalate to BLOCK.

would have caught defect #5 (and possibly defect #1 by the same logic) pre-merge.

## Updated priority recommendation

This bug now has 5 corpus examples, every prediction validated, and two remediation directions empirically pinned to specific deep-tier review prompts. Promoting from P1 to **immediate-action** on directions #3 and #6 is now defensible from the corpus alone.

comments.body:
Investigation complete. ROOT_CAUSE confirmed via static analysis of all affected files.

**Root cause**: Four distinct but related behavioral gaps in agent/skill instruction files that collectively allow VALIDATION-CLASS epics to close P1=PASS without environment-faithful integration test coverage.

Gap 1 (story-decomposer.md): No requirement exists to map LIVE-VERIFIED/VALIDATION-CLASS SCs to DDs that exercise the production environment shape. The Done Definitions rubric (Step 5) only requires DDs be 'measurable' and trace to an SC — nothing enforces that a LIVE-VERIFIED SC requires an environment-isolated integration test DD.

Gap 2 (behavioral-testing-standard.md): Rules 1-5 say nothing about environment-state-absent cases. Specifically: when code under test consumes runtime environment state (git config, mounted worktrees, env vars, file presence), no rule requires a test case where that state is explicitly absent. The standard only covers: existing coverage check, observable behavior, execute-don't-inspect, refactoring litmus, and structural boundary for instruction files.

Gap 3 (code-reviewer-deep-verification.md): The Python test pattern section mentions tmp_path and monkeypatch for filesystem isolation, but no checklist item asks 'does this test assume dev-machine state (global git config, pre-existing worktrees, env vars) that CI does not provide?' The NOT-flag rules actively discourage flagging test environment gaps as 'important' without a concrete failure path — which environment-divergence gaps don't always have until they hit CI.

Gap 4 (code-reviewer-deep-arch.md): No guidance for pre-existing test failures in VALIDATION-CLASS epics. The arch reviewer has no rule preventing 'pre-existing failure' framing from being accepted as a PASS rationale when the failing tests are in a load-bearing path for the epic's live-evidence claim.

hypothesis_tests:
- verified story-decomposer.md: zero mentions of LIVE, VALIDATION, live_verified, environment-isolated — CONFIRMED GAP
- verified behavioral-testing-standard.md: no Rule 6, no environment-state-absent rule — CONFIRMED GAP  
- verified code-reviewer-deep-verification.md: only tmp_path/monkeypatch, no dev-machine-state-divergence check — CONFIRMED GAP
- verified code-reviewer-deep-arch.md: no pre-existing-failure/VALIDATION-CLASS guidance — CONFIRMED GAP
- verified completion-verifier.md: observable-behavior criteria require execution trace (correct), but story-trust chain (Step 3a) propagates story-level PASS without rechecking if DDs actually exercised live env — PARTIAL gap (less critical than other 4)
comments.author: Test

comments.body: Anti-pattern scan: confirmed root-cause pattern is unique to story-decomposer.md DD-rubric and behavioral-testing-standard.md (no environment-absent-state rule). The reviewer agent delta files (deep-verification, deep-arch) were also anti-pattern candidates and have been patched. No other agents/skills share the same structural gap — task-decomposer inherits DDs from story-decomposer and does not author them; completion-verifier observable-behavior criteria already require execution traces for live-verified criteria. Observation: the defect class is localized to the planning → DD rubric pipeline, not the execution agents.
